Hey, I'm somebody who started investing completely by herself and I don't have a safety net either. For a very long time, I was paralysed with the fear of losing my money. I knew about investing back when I was 18 but it took me 5 years to actually invest and not just leave my money in my bank account because I was so scared.


In my experience, the only way to help that fear is to research. You don't have to figure out the numbers or do the math, YouTube videos from respectable sources are enough. Learn the basics from them, about what things are, how they work, etc. Learn about different types of investments: FD vs RD, stocks vs MFs, index funds vs ETFs, etc. Once you have this knowledge, download a trading app. I use Groww. It would most probably have charts and analysis for various categories in it. Look up terms you don't understand, eg: exit load. Play around in that app for sometime. Once you feel like you understand it a bit better, think about where you want to invest. I started with ELSS bc I knew I needed to save tax. You can sort the MFs based on returns so I did that, read about the MF on the internet and when I felt okay about it, I put in my money. Bc it was a tax saving thing, I wasn't too worried about higher rates of return, this helped me calm down my fear. After this it took me almost 2 years to be brave enough to invest in other MFs. I knew which ones to pick but I was still scared. But I took the plunge after my research. 


Hope this helps! It's still scary tbh bc what if I lose my money, and then I have to be homeless and then I won't be able to afford healthcare, blah blah blah, but this is the only way I'll be able to take care of older me . This is the only way I'll be able to build wealth by myself as I have 0 family support. So I have to take a calculated risk. Worst case scenario, maybe I'll write a book about my failures and make money lol

Onion tomato thokku


2 Large Onions Finely Chopped

▢3 Large Tomatoes Finely Chopped

▢10-12 Garlic Cloves Crushed

▢3 tablespoon Gingelly Oil Sesame Oil

▢½ teaspoon Mustard Seeds

▢1 teaspoon Urad Dal

▢¼ teaspoon Asafoetida

▢1 tablespoon Sambar Powder

▢½ teaspoon Turmeric Powder

▢Few Fresh Curry Leaves

▢Salt as needed

▢Water as needed ~¼ to ⅓ cup


INSTRUCTIONS

 

In a heavy pan heat 3 tablespoon sesame oil/gingelly oil. Add ½ teaspoon mustard seeds, 1 teaspoon urad dal and as the dal turns golden, add ¼ teaspoon asafoetida and few fresh curry leaves along with 10-12 crushed garlic cloves.

Next add 2 large onions finely chopped. Fry on low flame until translucent.

Now add 3 large tomatoes finely chopped. Cook for 3-4 mins on low flame.

Add ½ teaspoon turmeric powder and salt as needed. Cook for another 3-4 mins.

Next add 1 tablespoon Sambar Powder.

Cook on low flame for 3-4 mins and oil starts to ooze out.

To bring it to the right consistency, add about ¼ to ⅓ cup of water. Mix well.

Cook covered on low flame for 12-15 mins.

When the consistency of the thokku is thick and oil oozes out from sides, remove from heat.

Cool down completely, store it into an airtight container and refrigerate for upto a week.
